display.title: Episode 236: The Drunken Father (The Three Weeks)
display.summary_short: During the Three Weeks: how Rabbi Akiva's negel vasser saved his life, why Ahavas Yisroel leads to love of Hashem, and a story with no happy ending about a boy and his drinking father.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the middle of the Three Weeks, without the usual march. Uncle Yossi invites children to join Tzivos Hashem, explaining that Torah and mitzvos are the secret weapon that defeats the yetzer hara. A girl from a Brooklyn Beis Yaakov leads the Shema, followed by a sponsor message. The first story: Rabbi Akiva, jailed for teaching Torah and given no water for three days, uses his jug of water to wash his hands and make a brachah; the amazed ruler frees him and makes him an advisor. Uncle Yossi then explains Rabbi Akiva's great rule, to love your fellow as yourself, and the Alter Rebbe's teaching that Ahavas Yisroel leads to love of Hashem, which matters most in the Three Weeks. The second story 'has no happy ending': Naftali, a fine boy, is ashamed that his father drinks; he leads him to a drunk lying in the street, but his father only asks where to get such a good drink. From Parshas Acharei: Hashem shows us other nations' ways only so we will not follow them. The show ends with a call to sign up new members for extra points.
display.lesson: Seeing the wrong ways of others should teach us not to copy them; love every Jew, and through that, love Hashem.

date.note: 'Now that we are in the middle of the Three Weeks'; Tuesday one week after episode 235 (15 Tammuz 5746). Weekly estimate was 1986-07-28.

advisories.note: A father's drinking problem; his son cries about it and fails to change him.
The story deliberately ends without the father changing.
Rabbi Akiva jailed for teaching Torah and left without water for three days.

privacy.note: Shema guest named in full, with her school.

sources_cited.note: 'Like the practice of the land of Egypt... you shall not do', from Parshas Acharei.
Rabbi Akiva's sayings 'as we find them in the Gemara'; loving your fellow is a great rule of the Torah.
The Alter Rebbe: Ahavas Yisroel leads to Ahavas Hashem.
